chronic_conditions: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (25-year duration, poorly controlled)

encounters.cc: progressive fatigue, numbness in feet, and trouble walking over the past several months

lines: Progressive fatigue, numbness in feet, and trouble walking over the past several months
Progressive fatigue, numbness in his feet, and trouble walking over the past several months.
He reports that he has also been experiencing occasional memory lapses and a sensation of "pins and needles" in his hands and legs.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (25-year duration, poorly controlled)
He was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes 8 years ago but has had poor follow-up and limited access to care.
- Insulin glargine 30 units subcutaneously at bedtime
He is originally from northern Europe and follows a vegan diet for ethical reasons and denies alcohol or tobacco use.
On examination, he is pale and appears mildly disoriented to date.
Neurologic exam shows decreased proprioception and vibration sense in both lower extremities, with a wide-based gait.
Hematologic labs reveal macrocytic anemia with a hemoglobin of 9.2 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume (MCV) of 112 fL.
Additional testing confirms a deficiency in a cofactor required for homocysteine remethylation.

encounters.cc: progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea over 2 months

lines: Progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea over 2 months
The patient returns for follow-up approximately one year after his prior encounter for vitamin B12 deficiency.
He presents with a 2-month history of progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea.
He denies chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (25-year duration, poorly controlled)
His medications include metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin.
- Insulin glargine 30 units subcutaneously at bedtime
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired postal worker.
On physical examination, his blood pressure is 140/85 mmHg, heart rate is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute.
Cardiac examination reveals a regular rhythm without murmurs, rubs, or gallops.
Lung fields are clear to auscultation bilaterally.

encounters.cc: progressively worsening difficulty initiating urination with slow stream and post-void dribbling over the past year

lines: Progressively worsening difficulty initiating urination with slow stream and post-void dribbling over the past year

The patient is a 67-year-old male with a 25-year history of poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus complicated by peripheral neuropathy, who was previously evaluated for vitamin B12 deficiency and chronic kidney disease, and now presents with urinary complaints.
Over the past year, he has noticed progressively worsening difficulty initiating urination and reports that his urine stream is slow and occasionally stops and starts.
He also describes frequent dribbling of urine, especially after he thinks he has finished voiding.
Sometimes he feels the urge to urinate but cannot empty his bladder completely.
Over the last few weeks, he has begun waking up multiple times at night with wet underwear but no awareness that he had urinated.
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (25-year duration, poorly controlled)
His past medical history is significant for poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus for over 15 years with known peripheral neuropathy and retinopathy.
He takes insulin and multiple oral antihyperglycemics but has missed several follow-up appointments.
- Insulin glargine 30 units subcutaneously at bedtime
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired postal worker.
He denies dysuria, suprapubic pain, fever, or hematuria.
On physical examination, the bladder is palpable above the pubic symphysis and mildly tender to percussion.
A focused neurologic exam shows decreased sensation in the lower extremities with diminished ankle reflexes bilaterally.
Post-void residual urine volume is measured at 360 mL.

encounters.cc: ongoing upper abdominal discomfort with early fullness and nausea

lines: Ongoing upper abdominal discomfort with early fullness and nausea

The patient is a 69-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes mellitus of 25 years duration complicated by peripheral neuropathy, retinopathy, chronic kidney disease, prior B12 deficiency, and neurogenic bladder, presenting with abdominal discomfort that began several months ago and has gradually worsened.
He describes the pain as dull and constant, located just below the breastbone, and notes that it seems to get worse after eating, leading him to reduce his food intake.
He reports early fullness and occasional episodes of nausea, although he has not vomited recently.
Over the last few months, he has unintentionally lost about 15 pounds.
- Neurogenic bladder due to sacral nerve root injury (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (25-year duration, poorly controlled)
- Insulin glargine 30 units subcutaneously at bedtime
Physical examination reveals mild epigastric tenderness but no palpable abdominal mass.
Cardiopulmonary and neurological exams are unremarkable.
Laboratory investigations are notable for mild iron-deficiency anemia, and liver enzymes are within normal limits.
An upper abdominal imaging study shows signs suggestive of delayed gastric emptying and focal narrowing near the distal stomach.
A biopsy reveals malignant transformation involving the pyloric region.

encounters.cc: 4-month history of continuous urinary leakage and incomplete bladder emptying

lines: 4-month history of continuous urinary leakage and incomplete bladder emptying

The patient is a 69-year-old male with a history of neurogenic bladder secondary to sacral nerve root injury initially evaluated in 2023, complicated by 25 years of poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus with peripheral neuropathy and recent diagnosis of gastric adenocarcinoma, who presents to the Emergency Department with progression of lower urinary tract symptoms.
He describes his leakage as continuous dribbling of urine even after voiding, accompanied by a persistent feeling of incomplete bladder emptying.
He reports that he frequently finds himself needing to change his underwear multiple times per day and that these symptoms have gradually worsened over time.
He denies any burning during urination, hematuria, or suprapubic pain.
He also notes that despite making frequent trips to the bathroom, he never feels fully relieved.
His wife mentions that he often has difficulty initiating urination and sometimes seems to have a prolonged delay before a strong stream begins.
On further questioning, he admits that he previously had episodes suggestive of urinary retention, for which he was intermittently catheterized in the past.
- Neurogenic bladder due to sacral nerve root injury (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (25-year duration, poorly controlled)
- Insulin glargine 30 units subcutaneously at bedtime
Smoking: Never smoker. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Retired postal worker.
His physical exam reveals a soft, non-tender abdomen with a palpable lower abdominal mass that is consistent with bladder distension.
Digital rectal examination shows a normal-sized, smooth prostate.
Neurologic examination reveals decreased sensation in the feet and legs, consistent with diabetic peripheral neuropathy.
Laboratory studies reveal an HbA1c of 9.2% and normal renal function.
A bladder ultrasound confirms a post-void residual volume of 450 mL, indicating significant urinary retention.
